summary: The one-character `>`→`>=` change correctly fixes the mincnt>=1 inconsistency, but because the preceding `if mincnt is None: mincnt = 0` is left unchanged, the default case (mincnt unspecified, C provided) now evaluates `len(acc) >= 0`, which is always true and invokes reduce_C_function on empty bins. This regresses the documented 'at least one datum' default and breaks/changes behavior for empty cells.

issues.description: The original `len(acc) > mincnt` with `mincnt=0` (the None default) also served as an empty-bin guard. After the change, mincnt=None→0 yields `len(acc) >= 0`, which is always True, so reduce_C_function is now called on empty bins. With np.sum this draws empty cells as 0 instead of hiding them (a visible default-behavior change — and the issue's own repro uses np.sum); with np.max/np.min it raises ValueError on empty arrays; with np.mean it emits RuntimeWarnings. This is a concrete regression in the default (mincnt unspecified) C-provided path.

Fix is incomplete. It only makes mincnt>=1 consistent but mishandles the None/0 default. A correct fix must preserve the 'at least one datum' default when mincnt is None (e.g. set `mincnt = 1` for the None case, or keep an explicit non-empty guard) while using `>=` for explicit mincnt values.

Single-character flip is fragile: it conflates two distinct semantics (the empty-bin guard and the threshold comparison) that the original code combined in one `>` expression, so changing only the operator silently removes the guard for the default path.
